scalesUsed.notes: F - G - A - Bb - C - D - E - F
scalesUsed.application: Primary harmonic foundation for all chord progressions and vocal melody
Melodic hooks and simple lead guitar fills between vocal phrases

keyAndScale.modalCharacter: Ionian (Major) with a bright, driving pop-rock feel

mainProgression.description: Classic pop-rock progression that cycles through tonic, mediant minor, subdominant, and dominant chords, creating a satisfying and singable harmonic loop.

sectionProgressions.description: Driving verse progression with steady strumming that supports the storytelling vocal delivery
Building section using the relative minor to create tension before the chorus resolution
Anthemic chorus using the ubiquitous I-V-vi-IV progression that gives the song its memorable, uplifting quality

harmonicFunction: F (I) - Tonic chord establishing the bright major key center
Am (iii) - Mediant minor adding subtle darkness and movement in the verse
Bb (IV) - Subdominant providing warmth and forward harmonic motion
C (V) - Dominant chord creating tension and resolution back to tonic
Dm (vi) - Relative minor adding emotional depth in the pre-chorus

techniques.name: Basic Strumming Pattern
techniques.description: Steady eighth-note strumming pattern with accents on beats 2 and 4 that drives the song's pop-rock energy throughout all sections

notes: F: 1-3-3-2-1-1 (standard F barre chord) or X-X-3-2-1-1 (simplified mini-barre)
Am: X-0-2-2-1-0 (open Am shape)
Bb: X-1-3-3-3-1 (Bb barre chord) or X-X-3-3-3-1 (simplified)
C: X-3-2-0-1-0 (open C shape)
Dm: X-X-0-2-3-1 (open Dm shape)
Strumming pattern: Down-Down-Up-Up-Down-Up in eighth note feel
Accent the backbeats (beats 2 and 4) for pop-rock groove
sequence: Start with the simplified F chord (no full barre) if needed
Establish the strumming pattern on F for one full bar
Transition to Am on the downbeat of the next bar
Continue pattern through Bb and C to complete the verse cycle
tips: If the F barre chord is too difficult, use the simplified X-X-3-2-1-1 voicing
Keep the strumming hand moving in constant motion even during chord changes
Focus on smooth left-hand transitions rather than speed
The Bb chord can be simplified to X-1-3-3-3-X (omitting the high E string)
details.progression: F - Am - Bb - C (verse) / F - C - Dm - Bb (chorus)

techniques.name: Barre Chord Fundamentals
techniques.description: Introduction to barre chords through the F and Bb shapes used in this song, a critical technique for developing guitar players

notes: F barre chord: index finger barres all 6 strings at 1st fret, major shape on top
Bb barre chord: index finger barres strings at 1st fret, A-shape barre
Simplified F: X-X-3-2-1-1 (just the top four strings)
Simplified Bb: X-1-3-3-3-X (partial barre, omit outer strings)
Apply even pressure across the barre with the side of the index finger
Position the index finger close to the fret wire for cleanest tone
sequence: Start with the simplified F and Bb shapes to build confidence
Practice forming the full F barre chord and strumming each string individually
Work on transitioning from open shapes (Am, C) to barre shapes (F, Bb)
Gradually increase the speed of transitions
Incorporate full barre chords into the strumming pattern
tips: Use the bony side edge of your index finger, not the soft pad
Keep your thumb centered on the back of the neck for leverage
Don't press harder than necessary - proper finger placement reduces effort
If strings buzz, adjust finger position rather than applying more pressure
Take breaks to avoid hand fatigue while building barre chord strength

techniques.name: Pre-Chorus Build
techniques.description: Gradually increasing strumming intensity through the pre-chorus section to create energy that launches into the anthemic chorus

notes: Start the pre-chorus at moderate volume (mf)
Gradually increase strumming width and attack through the section
Add more strings to each strum as intensity builds
By the end of the pre-chorus, strum with full arm motion
The dynamic build mirrors the vocal melody's rising energy
sequence: Begin Dm with controlled wrist strumming
Increase strum width on the C chord
Open up fully on Bb with broader arm motion
Hit the final C before the chorus with maximum energy
Explode into the F chord on the chorus downbeat
tips: Think of the dynamic build as a gradual slope, not a sudden jump
Use more of your forearm as the intensity increases
The audience should feel the energy building before the chorus arrives
Practice the crescendo with a metronome to avoid rushing

sections.name: Intro
sections.description: Clean guitar intro establishing the rhythmic feel and chord progression before vocals enter
notes: Moderate strumming intensity to set the tone
Clean electric guitar tone with slight compression
Establish the tempo at 98 BPM from the first strum
One cycle of the chord progression before verse begins

sections.name: Verse
sections.description: Steady verse strumming supporting the narrative vocal melody with the main I-iii-IV-V progression
notes: Consistent strumming pattern throughout the verse
Keep dynamics at a moderate level to leave room for the chorus
Focus on clean chord transitions, especially to the Bb barre chord
The Am provides a brief minor color before resolving through Bb to C

sections.name: Pre-Chorus
sections.description: Building section with the relative minor (Dm) creating tension and increasing energy toward the chorus
notes: Begin building intensity from the Dm chord
The minor chord shift creates emotional tension
Gradually increase strumming volume and attack
Arrive at the final C chord with full energy ready for the chorus

sections.name: Chorus
sections.description: Anthemic chorus with the iconic I-V-vi-IV progression and full-energy strumming behind the memorable vocal hook
notes: Full strumming intensity for the chorus
The I-V-vi-IV progression drives the singalong quality
Emphasize the downbeat of each chord change
Maintain high energy throughout the entire chorus section

sections.name: Outro
sections.description: Repeated chorus progression with gradual fadeout, maintaining energy to the end of the song
notes: Repeating chorus progression drives the song to conclusion
Keep strumming consistent as the song fades
The energy should feel sustained rather than diminishing
Final resolution lands on the F tonic chord

guitar.recommended: Fender Telecaster or clean-toned electric guitar
guitar.pickup: Bridge pickup or bridge+middle position for bright, clean pop tone

amp.recommended: Fender Twin Reverb or similar clean amp

effects.delay: Very subtle short delay for depth
effects.reverb: Light spring or plate reverb for polish
effects.other: Light compression pedal for consistent strumming volume. No heavy effects needed.

beginner.focus: Learn the open chord shapes and basic strumming pattern
steps: Master Am, C, and Dm open chord shapes
Learn the simplified F chord voicing (X-X-3-2-1-1)
Learn the simplified Bb chord voicing (X-1-3-3-3-X)
Practice the basic down-up strumming pattern at slow tempo

intermediate.focus: Master full barre chords and play through the complete song structure
steps: Work on the full F barre chord shape
Practice the full Bb barre chord shape
Play the verse, pre-chorus, and chorus progressions at 98 BPM
Add the dynamic build through the pre-chorus section

advanced.focus: Polish dynamics, add embellishments, and sing along
steps: Add subtle strumming variations for interest between sections
Practice singing while strumming the full arrangement
Experiment with different voicings and inversions for variety
Perform the complete song with authentic dynamic arc

commonMistakes: Stopping the strumming hand during barre chord transitions
Pressing too hard on barre chords causing hand fatigue
Playing the verse and chorus at the same dynamic level
Rushing through the pre-chorus build instead of gradually increasing intensity
practiceRoutine: Warm up by practicing full barre chord shapes (F and Bb) for 5 minutes
Work on transitions between open and barre chords at slow tempo
Play through the verse progression (F-Am-Bb-C) with the strumming pattern
Practice the pre-chorus build from soft to loud over 4 bars
Run through the complete song structure at 98 BPM
focusAreas: Clean barre chord formations with no buzzing strings
Smooth transitions between open and barre chord shapes
Consistent strumming rhythm throughout chord changes
Dynamic contrast between verse and chorus sections
metronomeWork: Start at 70 BPM with just chord changes on each beat
Add the strumming pattern at 70 BPM, increasing by 5 BPM increments
Practice at 98 BPM (song tempo) with full strumming pattern
Use metronome on beats 2 and 4 for pop-rock backbeat feel
